correctness.rationale: De Finetti reduces the problem to maximizing E f(P) over laws on [0,1] with E P=mu, where f(p)=C(n,k)p^k(1-p)^(n-k). The ratios f(p)/p and f(p)/(1-p) have unique maxima at a=(k-1)/(n-1) and b=k/(n-1). Their tangent chords meet f with matching slopes. The explicit second-derivative quadratic is nonpositive on [a,b], proving central concavity; the chord argument proves the resulting function is the least concave majorant. The greatest convex minorant is zero because f vanishes at both endpoints. Explicit one/two-atom directing laws attain every boundary piece and convex mixing fills the interval. An independently written exact-rational grid replay verified f<=U for n<=30 and all interior k.
risks: Endpoint counts k=0,n are intentionally excluded and have different one-sided geometry.

value.rationale: Exact-count probabilities are natural local concentration statistics in exchangeable binary and random-effects models. The theorem gives the full attainable interval and explicit extremizers, and identifies exactly when the iid law is or is not optimal.
risks: Additional constraints on the directing law, such as a fixed variance, would change the envelope.

final_claim: For an infinitely exchangeable Bernoulli sequence with marginal mean mu, the attainable probability of exactly k successes in n trials, 1<=k<=n-1, is exactly [0,U_{n,k}(mu)], where U is the stated three-piece least-concave-majorant formula with breakpoints (k-1)/(n-1) and k/(n-1).
limitations: Only the directing mean is fixed.
